MRW5. Certificate of Sponsorship for the religious work routes

This section tells you how to assign a valid Certificate of Sponsorship to a worker on the Minister of Religion and Religious Worker routes.

Overview

MRW5.1. If you have followed all the rules in this guidance and you wish to sponsor a worker on the Minister of Religion route or Religious Worker route, you must assign them a valid Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS), using your sponsorship management system (SMS) account.

MRW5.2. Before assigning a CoS, you should satisfy yourself that the worker can meet the relevant immigration requirements.

MRW5.3. You must normally be an A-rated sponsor to assign a CoS. You can only assign a CoS as a B-rated sponsor if all of the following are true:

the worker is applying for permission to stay on the same route as in their last grant of permission

you sponsored the application which led to that grant of permission

the worker will be paid at least National Minimum Wage for their role

For more information on sponsor ratings, see section L8 of Part 1: Apply for a licence.

MRW5.4. For detailed information on what a CoS is, and how many you can assign, see section S2 of Part 2: Sponsor a worker.

MRW5.5. You can find detailed technical guidance on how to assign a CoS on GOV.UK: User manuals: sponsorship management system (SMS) – see in particular manual 8.

Fees

MRW5.6. You must pay a fee for each CoS you assign. The amount you pay will depend on which route you are sponsoring the worker – see UK visa fees on GOV.UK for information on current fee levels.

MRW5.7. For CoS assigned to Ministers of Religion on or after 9 April 2025, you must not recoup, or attempt to recoup, by any means, any part of the CoS fee, or associated administrative costs, from any workers you sponsor. If we find you have done this, we will normally revoke your licence.

Use of the CoS

MRW5.8. Once you have assigned a CoS, the worker must use it within 3 months to apply for:

entry clearance (a visa) if they are outside the UK

permission to stay if they are in the UK and eligible to extend their stay on the Minister of Religion or Religious Worker route or switch (change) from another route to the Minister of Religion route

MRW5.9. If the CoS was issued more than 3 months before the date of application, we may reject their application and not consider it.

MRW5.10. The worker must not apply for a visa or permission to stay more than 3 months before the start date recorded on their CoS. If they do, we will refuse their application.

MRW5.11. We will also refuse the application if the CoS:

has been withdrawn by you or cancelled by the Home Office – see section S6 of Part 2: Sponsor a worker for information on when a CoS can be withdrawn or cancelled

was used in a previous application that was refused

What the CoS must confirm

MRW5.12. For a CoS to be valid on these routes, it must meet the requirements of the relevant Immigration Rules:

Minister of Religion: paragraphs MOR 5.1 to MOR 5.4 of Appendix T2 Minister of Religion

Religious Worker: paragraphs RW 4.1 to RW 4.6 of Appendix Temporary Work - Religious Worker

MRW5.13. By assigning a CoS on these routes, you are guaranteeing that:

the role is eligible to be sponsored on the Minister of Religion or Religious Worker route (as appropriate)

the worker is qualified to do the job in question

the worker will receive pay and conditions at least equal to those given to settled workers in the same role, and the role will comply with both the National Minimum Wage Regulations and the Working Time Regulations

the worker will comply with their conditions of stay – see section S8 of Part 2: Sponsor a worker for more information

MRW5.14. In addition, by assigning a CoS to a Minister of Religion, you guarantee that:

the worker will perform religious duties within your organisation or as directed by your organisation in the UK (which may include preaching, pastoral and non-pastoral work)

the worker’s role will not involve mainly non-pastoral duties, such as school teaching, media production, domestic work or administrative and clerical work, unless the role is a senior position within your organisation or they are a member of a religious order

MRW5.15. The CoS must confirm all of the following:

that you are sponsoring the worker on the Minister of Religion or Religious Worker route, as appropriate

the worker’s personal information (such as name, date of birth, nationality), passport details and contact details

the start and end date of their employment – see section S3 of Part 2: sponsor a worker for information on start and end dates

where the worker will carry out their employment – this should include their main work address and any other regular work addresses, if relevant

whether you used an agent (such as a recruitment agency, employment business or other intermediary) to find the worker and, if so, details of that agent

the job title

the relevant SOC 2020 occupation code (select from the drop-down list under ‘Job type’ – for Ministers of Religion, this will normally be 2463 (clergy)) – see section S3 of Part 2: Sponsor a worker for further information on occupation codes

the main duties of the role for which the worker is being sponsored

the worker’s gross salary (including any guaranteed allowances and bonuses)

the worker’s religion

Eligible Religious Worker roles

MRW3.6. The Religious Worker route is for people coming to the UK for a temporary period (of up to 24 months) to support the activities of religious institutions. The role must involve performing religious duties within, or directed by, the sponsor, including:

non-pastoral placements within a religious organisation

as a member of a religious order – members of a religious order can also be sponsored on the Minister of Religion route

MRW3.7. You must not use the Religious Worker route to fill the role of a minister of religion. If you wish to sponsor a minister of religion, you must do so on the Minister of Religion route.

MRW3.8. There is no longer a resident labour consideration requirement on the Religious Worker route if the worker applied for entry clearance or permission on or after 29 October 2026. Religious Workers must instead meet one of the following requirements:

the role is supernumerary (see paragraphs MRW3.13 to MRW3.14)

the worker will mainly live within and be a member of a religious order – for example, an order of nuns or monks (sees paragraphs MRW3.4 to MRW3.5)

the worker performed religious duties outside the UK for the same faith-based organisation to which you are affiliated for at least 6 months immediately prior to the date of application – the worker must provide evidence of this with their application for entry clearance or permission

the worker is applying for permission to stay from within the UK and you sponsored the application which led to their last grant of permission on the Religious Worker route

MRW3.9. When you assign a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS) to a Religious Worker, you must give an explanation (either in the job description field or by adding a sponsor note) of how the job meets the above requirements. If the role is supernumerary, you must clearly explain how it is supernumerary – it is not sufficient simply to say the job is supernumerary. If you fail to give this information, the worker’s application may be delayed or refused.

MRW3.10. If the worker applied for entry clearance or permission before 29 October 2026, you must be able to show how you satisfied the resident labour consideration, unless the worker or role was exempt from that requirement. See the relevant archived version of this guidance for further information.

MRW3.11. If you assigned the relevant CoS before 29 October 2026 but the worker applies on or after that date, you must add a sponsor note if, at the time you assigned the CoS, the resident labour consideration was met because you either:

identified the worker from national records you hold of all available workers

advertised the role

MRW3.12. You must explain in the sponsor note how the worker meets the new role eligibility requirements described in paragraph MRW3.8.

Meaning of ‘supernumerary’

MRW3.13. A role is supernumerary if it is over and above your normal staffing requirements. This means that if the person filling the role were not there, it wouldn’t be filled by anyone else – for example, where the worker offers pastoral support to members of a church community as part of their own development, but the work would stop if they were not there and you wouldn’t replace them

MRW3.14. A position that is not supernumerary is one that is vital to the normal work of your organisation. Examples include, but are not limited to:

a translator of religious texts working for a missionary organisation – if that person left, but there was still a need for a translator, the role is not supernumerary

a choir director, worship musician or ceremonial assistant filling an established role in regular services – if you would need another person to perform those duties if the worker left, the role is not supernumerary

Pay and conditions for the religious work routes

MRW3.15. You must ensure any worker you sponsor on the religious work routes will receive pay and conditions that are no less favourable than those given to settled workers doing the same role.

MRW3.16. In all cases, the role must comply with both the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 and the Working Time Regulations 1998 (unless an exemption in those regulations applies). We will refuse any application for entry clearance or permission to stay where we have reasonable grounds to believe the role does not comply with these regulations, and we will also consider revoking your sponsor licence. For further information, see section S4 of Part 2: Sponsor a worker.

MRW3.17. If you will not be paying the worker National Minimum Wage because of an exemption in the National Minimum Wage Regulations, you must include an explanation of this on the CoS. You can include this information either:

in the ‘Gross salary’ box when you are assigning the CoS

by adding a sponsor note after you have assigned the CoS

MRW3.18. If the worker will not be entitled to National Minimum Wage, you must confirm on the CoS that you will maintain and accommodate the worker (and their dependants, if relevant) for the duration of their permission in the UK. You must be an A-rated sponsor to do this.

MRW3.19. If an exemption does not apply, you must ensure the worker receives at least National Minimum Wage. You cannot refuse to pay National Minimum Wage just because (for example) the worker can support themselves out of their own funds or from donations.

MRW1. Sponsoring a person on the religious work routes: overview

This section provides an overview of the Minister of Religion and Religious Worker routes, the sponsorship requirements you must meet, and other ways religious workers can come to the UK.

What are the religious work routes?

MRW1.1. There are two main routes on which you can sponsor people to work in religious occupations:

Minister of Religion: this route is for the recruitment of a person who has a key leading role within their religious establishment or organisation in the UK, such as a minister of religion, missionary, or other religious workers in mainly pastoral roles; it is also for members of religious orders

Religious Worker: this route is for people who want to support the activities of religious institutions in the UK by conducting religious work, such as working in a religious order or filling non-pastoral placements, for no more than 2 years

MRW1.2. The table below provides a summary of the main differences between the two routes. See sections MRW3 and MRW4 for detailed information. It is your responsibility to ensure you apply for a licence and the sponsor the worker on the correct route:

Requirement Minister of Religion Religious Worker

Eligible employment Work must be of a mainly pastoral nature, such as leading a congregation in performing rites and rituals, and preaching the essentials of the creed – for example, religious leaders such as priests, imams, rabbis and other ministers of religion. It can also be used by missionaries and members of religious orders. Work can involve performing religious duties to support the activities of religious institutions and can be either pastoral or non-pastoral. It can include working in a religious order. You must not use this route to sponsor ministers of religion.

English language Applicants must meet an English language requirement. No English language requirement.

‘Switching’ immigration route while in the UK Applicants already in the UK on another immigration route can ‘switch’ to the Minister of Religion route (with certain exceptions). Switching not permitted.

Maximum initial period of permission Up to 3 years. Up to 24 months.

Maximum overall stay None. May be eligible to apply for settlement (indefinite leave to remain) after 5 years on this route. Maximum stay of 24 months with no option to apply for settlement.

‘Cooling-off’ period None. Applicants outside the UK are not eligible to apply for 12 months (known as the cooling-off period) if they’ve been in the UK as a Religious Worker or Charity Worker in the last 12 months.
